Yorkshire Dales: England's Green and Pleasant Riding

The Yorkshire Dales is a gentler riding experience than the Lake District or Scotland, but no less rewarding. Rolling green valleys, drystone walls stretching to the horizon, charming stone villages, and roads that flow perfectly with the landscape — it's motorcycling as therapy. The Dales reward a relaxed pace and an appreciation for understated beauty.

The Classic Dales Loop

Start from Skipton, the gateway to the Dales, and head north through Wharfedale to Kettlewell. From there, climb over the exposed moorland to Coverdale and descend to Middleham. Continue through Wensleydale to Hawes, then over the Buttertubs Pass to Swaledale. Return via Richmond and the A6108 through Masham. This 130-mile loop takes in the best of the Dales.

Buttertubs Pass

The Buttertubs Pass between Hawes and Thwaite is the Yorkshire Dales' most famous road. Named after the limestone potholes beside the road, it climbs to 526 metres through open moorland. The pass was featured in the 2014 Tour de France and offers sweeping bends with views across Swaledale. The surface is generally good but can be exposed to crosswinds.

Fleet Moss

Fleet Moss is the highest road in the Dales at 589 metres. The climb from Hawes is relentless — 25% gradients on a narrow road through bleak moorland. It's a proper challenge and the views from the top across Wharfedale are the reward. The descent to Buckden is fast and flowing.

The Yorkshire Dales is England at its most photogenic. Drystone walls, barns, and bridges create a landscape that hasn't changed in centuries. Slow down and soak it in.

Best Dales Roads

  • B6160 through Wharfedale — Green valley road following the River Wharfe, gentle and beautiful
  • B6255 Ribblehead — Passes under the famous Ribblehead Viaduct, dramatic moorland
  • B6270 Swaledale — Perhaps the most beautiful of all the Dales, quiet and unspoiled
  • Tan Hill to Reeth — Wild road via Britain's highest pub at Tan Hill Inn

Biker-Friendly Stops

The Dales is blessed with excellent pubs. The Tan Hill Inn (Britain's highest pub at 528m) is a must-visit. The Wensleydale Creamery in Hawes is perfect for a cheese-and-tea stop. The Dales Bike Centre near Reeth is a dedicated motorcyclist haven with cafe, camping, and workshop facilities. Hawes, Settle, and Richmond all have fuel stations.

When to Ride

The Dales are at their best from late April to October. Lambing season (April-May) means slow down for sheep on roads. August brings heather blooming on the moors — the purple landscape is stunning. Autumn colours in October are spectacular. Winter riding is possible but higher passes can be icy and closed after snow.
keyTakeaways: The classic 130-mile Dales loop from Skipton links Wharfedale, Wensleydale, Buttertubs and Swaledale.
Buttertubs Pass climbs to 526 metres between Hawes and Thwaite and featured in the 2014 Tour de France.
Fleet Moss is the highest road in the Dales at 589 metres, with relentless 25% gradients from Hawes.
Biker-friendly stops include the Tan Hill Inn, Britain's highest pub at 528 metres, and the Dales Bike Centre near Reeth.
Best ridden late April to October; lambing season means slowing for sheep, and August brings blooming heather.
